items.q: What does a Berlin Wall map overlay show?
items.a: It places the 1989 border line on top of the present-day map. A good overlay tells you which side of the Wall a specific point was on, East, West, or on the border itself, and how far that point sat from the actual fortification, accurate to within a few metres using the city's survey records.

items.q: Is there a Berlin Wall Google Street View?
items.a: No, because the Wall is gone in almost every central location, so there is nothing standing to see in a street view. An overlay is more useful for a visit: it tells you where the line was so you can stand on the spot and look for the cobblestone trace and bronze plaques yourself.

items.q: How do I use the overlay while walking in Berlin?
items.a: Tap your current location or type a street, read whether it was East or West, check the distance to the line, and watch for the on the Wall itself result within 25 metres of the border. It takes about ten seconds per spot and turns the map from a picture into a tool.

items.q: How accurate are these Wall overlays?
items.a: The reliable ones build the border line from the city's own surveying records rather than drawing it by hand, so they are accurate to within a few metres. That is why they can flag any point within 25 metres of the line as on the Wall itself, where the boundary and the real fortification overlap.
